title: In an abstract Setoid-flavored ring, an element minus itself is equivalent to zero
statement: For any AlgS.Ring record R and any x of R's carrier, equiv (AlgS.sub R x x) zero, where AlgS.sub R a b := add a (neg b) -- proved by negAdd x alone, since AlgS.sub R x x beta+delta-unfolds to add x (neg x), exactly negAdd's own stated conclusion.

formal.statement: theorem AlgS.sub_self : ((x0 : AlgS.Ring) -> ((x1 : AlgS.Ring.carrier x0) -> AlgS.Ring.equiv x0 (AlgS.sub x0 x1 x1) (AlgS.Ring.zero x0)))

evidence.supports: AlgS.sub_self admits through the trusted kernel gate and type-checks fully applied, both instantiated at CReal.commRingS's AlgS.CommRing.toRingS projection and at AlgS.Ring.ofAlg(Int.ring) (concrete at the respective zero element and symbolic, closed via lam_over). CReal/Int have no named `sub_self` kernel theorem to compare against, so this is a well-typedness measurement.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(RUST_MIN_STACK=1073741824 cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib --release -- sub_self_instantiated_at_int_through_ofalg_concrete_and_symbolic generic_sub_self_instantiated_at_creal_type_checks_concrete_and_symbolic --test-threads=1 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -cE 'test result: ok\. 2 passed; 0 failed')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pinned pattern requires BOTH counts ('2 passed; 0 failed') across both instantiation-site tests.

notes: The Setoid-flavored analogue of Alg.sub/Alg.sub_self (ADR-1584); the proof is the same beta+delta-unfold trick, unaffected by the switch from Eq to equiv since the unfold happens purely at the definitional level before the law is even consulted.
